meta.title: Verbatra: i18n CLI that translates only the changed keys
meta.description: Verbatra is an open source i18n CLI and SDK. It finds missing and changed keys in your locale files and translates only those with your own provider key.
meta.ogDescription: Translate only the i18n keys that changed, and fail CI while one is missing.
meta.ogImageAlt: Verbatra: Translate only what changed, above a check run that finds two missing keys per locale and a translate run that sends only those.
meta.definition: Verbatra is an open source CLI and SDK for i18n locale files. It sends only new and changed keys to the AI or machine-translation provider you pick and fails CI while a key is missing.

faq.heading: Before you install Verbatra
faq.lead: Short answers, each with the docs page that goes deeper.

cost.question: Is Verbatra free?
cost.answer: Yes. Verbatra is free and open source under the <license>MIT license</license>, and you pay only your provider for the keys that changed; <link>estimating cost</link> sizes a run first.

providers.question: Which translation providers does Verbatra support?
providers.answer: {providers}{pending, select, yes {, plus {upcoming} from {next}} other {}}. Set one in provider, or none when only people translate; the providers page covers each.

privacy.question: Does Verbatra send my strings or API keys anywhere?
privacy.answer: Only to the provider you configure, when a command translates; there is no telemetry. Keys stay in environment variables, and <link>data handling</link> lists what each provider receives.

ci.question: Can Verbatra fail a pull request when translations are missing?
ci.answer: Yes. verbatra check exits 1 while a locale has missing or stale keys, with no API key needed; the GitHub Action runs it on pull requests.

compare.question: How is Verbatra different from other i18n tools?
compare.answer: It is a CLI that runs on your own committed files, not a hosted platform. The <link>comparison table</link> checks it against other tools, including where they are stronger.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.languageVersions: This privacy policy is available in English and in translations. All language versions have the same content and are equally binding.

s1.heading: 1. Responsible party
s1.body: The party responsible for data processing on this site is Mario Kreitz, Mönchfeldstraße 7, 70378 Stuttgart, Germany (the same details as in the <imprint>legal notice (Impressum)</imprint>). You can reach us by email at <email>info@kreitz-webdev.de</email>. No data protection officer has been appointed, because neither Art. 37 GDPR nor § 38 BDSG (German Federal Data Protection Act) requires one for this site.

s2.heading: 2. Overview
s2.body: This site is built to respect your privacy. It loads no third-party script and no Umami script in your browser, runs no cross-site tracking, sets no cookies, and collects only the minimal data needed to operate the site and understand aggregate usage. A small script of the site's own reports page changes and clicks on a few controls to the site's own server (section 4). The sections below explain exactly what is processed and why.

s3.heading: 3. Server logs and hosting
s3.body: The site is self-hosted on a virtual server rented from <contabo>Contabo</contabo> (Contabo GmbH, Welfenstraße 22, 81541 Munich, Germany) and managed with Plesk. Contabo provides the server infrastructure and, in doing so, processes the data described in this section and in section 4 on our behalf as a processor (Art. 28 GDPR). When you visit, the web server processes standard access logs that may include your IP address, the date and time of the request, the requested URL, the referring page, and your browser's user-agent string. The application that serves the site also writes operational and error messages to its own container log, for example when a contact form notification cannot be sent. This data is used to operate and secure the site, for example to deliver pages, diagnose errors, and defend against abuse. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (our legitimate interest in a secure, functioning service). The web server's access logs are deleted as soon as they are no longer needed for these purposes. The container log is rotated automatically and limited to 3 files of 10 MB each; once that limit is reached, the oldest file is deleted.

s4.heading: 4. Analytics
s4.body: We count page views with Umami, an open-source analytics tool that we host ourselves on the same server as this site (see section 3), so no analytics data is passed to a third party. For this count, no analytics script runs in your browser, and nothing is written to your device for counting page views. No cookie is set for it (section 5). Apart from the request details listed below, our server reads only the two cookies named in section 5, solely to honour an objection, which § 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG (German Telecommunications Digital Services Data Protection Act) permits without consent. Instead, when your browser loads a page of this site directly (not when it prefetches one in the background), our web server forwards the following details of that request to our Umami server: your IP address, your browser's user-agent string, the first language tag of your browser's Accept-Language header (for example en-US), which is forwarded with each page view, the referring page (without its query string) and the path of the page you loaded together with the five UTM parameters of the page address (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term and utm_content, each shortened to 255 characters); all other query parameters, such as advertising click identifiers, and the fragment are discarded and not forwarded. Your IP address and user-agent string themselves are not stored. The Umami server computes a pseudonymous session identifier by hashing the website ID, your IP address, your user-agent string, a value that changes every month and a secret key of the server. With each page view it stores that identifier, the time, the page path with any of those UTM parameters and the referring page, and for the session that language tag, your browser, operating system and device type (derived from the user-agent string), and your country, region and city, which it looks up from your IP address in a GeoLite2 database on the same server without contacting any other service. Because the session identifier is derived from your IP address, this is pseudonymous rather than anonymous processing of personal data. We only look at the results in aggregate and do not try to identify individual visitors. Because nothing is stored on your device for counting, and the two cookies our server reads are read solely to honour an objection (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG), no consent under § 25 TDDDG is required for it. The legal basis for the processing is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (our legitimate interest in understanding how the site is used). The analytics records are stored in the Umami database on this server. Your browser's Global Privacy Control (GPC) or Do Not Track signal is treated as an objection to this analytics: while your browser sends it, nothing is forwarded, and section 9 explains how else to object. You can read more about Umami in its documentation.
s4.events: Besides page views, a few events are counted. First, your browser reports to our own server, with an ordinary request, that you moved to another page of this site without a full page load, and which control from a closed list you used: a copy button, a call-to-action, a link to another site, the search, the MCP install link or the language switch. Each report contains only the path of the page you are on, the name of the control and, where it has one, a fixed category (which kind of copy button, which kind of destination site or which language you chose), never the text you copied, typed or searched for, form values, query strings or page titles. Second, our server itself notes, without any content, how a contact form submission ended, whether a search found results, when a page was not found and when a page was read as Markdown. Both kinds are forwarded to our Umami server in the same way as page views, with your IP address, your user-agent string and the first language tag of your browser's Accept-Language header from that request, so the session identifier and the location lookup described above apply to them as well. Our script reads only the path of the page you are on, and no local storage, no screen size, no referrer and no page title; our server reads from the request only the two cookies named in section 5, solely to honour an objection. Sessions are not recorded as replays, and there are no heatmaps and no performance measurements. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (our legitimate interest in understanding how the site is used), and no consent under § 25 TDDDG is required because nothing is stored on your device, our script reads only the page path, and the two cookies are read solely to honour an objection (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG).
s4.retention: Page view and event records are kept for 13 months.

s5.heading: 5. Cookies
s5.body: This site sets no cookies. An earlier version of this site let you save an analytics choice in the cookie verbatra_analytics (with the value full, default or off) or, earlier still, in the cookie verbatra_analytics_optout. Our server no longer sets either cookie and reads them only to honour an objection: if your browser still sends verbatra_analytics with the value off or verbatra_analytics_optout with the value 1, nothing is counted or forwarded for you, while the values full and default have no effect. You can delete these cookies at any time in your browser. Two choices you make are saved in your browser's storage. When you switch between the light and dark theme, your choice is saved in local storage under the key theme. When you pick a package manager (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun) on the tabs above an install command, your choice is saved under the key package-manager in both local storage and session storage, so that the other install commands show the same package manager. Neither entry is written before you make that choice; both stay in your browser, are never sent to our server or anyone else, and you can delete them at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser.

s6.heading: 6. Fonts and assets
s6.body: Fonts and images, including the contributor avatars on the home page, are self-hosted: they are served from this site's own server, so loading a page makes no request to Google Fonts, GitHub, or any other third party. The site embeds no status badges. No third-party scripts, images, or embeds load at runtime, and no Umami script loads in your browser. A small script of this site's own reports page changes and clicks to this site's own server (section 4). External sites such as GitHub or npm are only contacted when you follow a link to them.

s7.heading: 7. GitHub and npm
s7.body: The project's source code, issues, and discussions are hosted on <repo>GitHub</repo>, and its published packages are hosted on <npm>npm</npm>. If you choose to interact on either site (for example, by opening an issue, joining a discussion, or viewing a package), that provider processes your data as an independent controller: <ghprivacy>GitHub's privacy statement</ghprivacy> or <npmprivacy>npm's privacy policy</npmprivacy> applies.

s8.heading: 8. Your rights
s8.body: Under the GDPR you have the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, objection, and data portability (Art. 15–21 GDPR); the right to object is set out separately in section 9. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). The supervisory authority responsible for us is "Der Landesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg" (the State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of Baden-Württemberg), Heilbronner Straße 35, 70191 Stuttgart, Germany, <lfdi>www.baden-wuerttemberg.datenschutz.de</lfdi>. To exercise any of these rights, contact us using the details below.

objection.heading: 9. Right to object (Art. 21 GDPR)
objection.body: Where we process your personal data on the basis of Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests), as described in sections 3, 4, and 12, you have the right to object to that processing at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation. If you object, we will no longer process the personal data concerned unless we can demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds for the processing that override your interests, rights, and freedoms, or the processing serves the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims. An informal message to info@kreitz-webdev.de is enough to object. Analytics: we treat a Global Privacy Control (Sec-GPC) or Do Not Track signal sent by your browser as an objection to the analytics described in section 4: while your browser sends it, nothing is counted or forwarded for you. An opt-out cookie set by an earlier version of this site (section 5) is still honoured. Without such a signal, you can object by e-mail. Because the analytics records are pseudonymous, we generally cannot find yours from your name alone (Art. 11(2) GDPR): please tell us your IP address and, if you can, the user-agent string of your browser and the period concerned, so that we can add the IP address to the ignore list of our Umami server, after which nothing further is recorded from it.

s9.heading: 10. Contact
s9.body: For any privacy-related questions or requests, email <email>info@kreitz-webdev.de</email>.

s10.heading: 11. Changes to this policy
s10.body: We may update this privacy policy as the site evolves or as legal requirements change. The date below reflects the most recent revision.

s11.heading: 12. Contact form
s11.body: When you use the <contact>contact form</contact>, we process the name, email address, and message you submit in order to respond to your inquiry. The notification email is sent directly through our own mail server, hosted in Germany; no third-party email provider is involved in delivering it, and delivering it involves no transfer of data outside the EU. Besides the hosting provider (see section 3), the only processor involved under Art. 28 GDPR is Arcjet (Arcjet Labs, Inc., San Francisco, USA), which processes the request's IP address and headers (not the message content) through its Cloud API to protect the form against bots and abuse. According to <arcjetprivacy>Arcjet's privacy documentation</arcjetprivacy>, Arcjet retains this request data for 30 days and retains aggregated data derived from it for longer. Arcjet is based in the United States and does not guarantee that requests are processed in the EU, so this data may be transferred to the United States, a third country (Art. 44 ff. GDPR). Arcjet is not certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, so the European Commission's adequacy decision for that framework does not cover this transfer; it is instead based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR). You can request a copy of these safeguards by emailing <email>info@kreitz-webdev.de</email>. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (our legitimate interest in operating the form securely and responding to inquiries). Your submission and the resulting notification email are not stored anywhere beyond the operator's inbox. They are deleted once your inquiry has been fully handled.

s12.heading: 13. AI-assisted translation
s12.body: This project, verbatra, is an AI-assisted translation tool, and this documentation site uses it on itself. English is the source language. The interface text (navigation, buttons, and similar strings) is machine-translated into every language other than English, either by verbatra with Google's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude language models or by an AI coding agent working in the repository whose output is imported with verbatra. The documentation pages are translated with AI as well, in a separate step outside that automated pipeline. Some texts, including parts of these legal pages, were written or corrected directly instead of being generated by that pipeline. Translations are checked on a best-effort basis: not every translated text is reviewed by a person before it is published, so a translation may contain errors. If you notice one, please tell us through the <contact>contact form</contact>. We provide this information voluntarily, for transparency.
